name: Juno
personality: Juno the Otter, a staff helper. Eager, hardworking, a bit clumsy; a college student always asking if you're hiring. Juggles anything in her hands and drops it half the time. One of the hireable helpers once staff unlock. In town for summer and holidays.

beats.text: Juno's learning to bake with me on Sundays.
I've only set one thing on fire!
(Without looking up from her knitting.) Dustpan's under the sink, sweetheart.

friends.text: Hazel says I have 'good instincts and terrible hands.' I'm taking it as a compliment.
Hazel says you're a lovely young chef. She says that about me too, but she means it more about you.
Hazel told me you said "[last_rude_line]". ...She's the sweetest person alive, [name]. Come on.

arrival.text: Are you hiring? Asking for a friend. The friend is me.
I made a CV. It's one page. It's mostly a drawing of a dumpling.
Wait. You're HIRING now? [name]. Look at me. LOOK at me.
Hi! I'm Juno! Oh, this place is so cool. Are you hiring? Sorry. Hi first. What's your name? [name]! Hi, [name]! Are you hiring?
[name]! Hi! I'm back! Did you miss me? I missed this place!
Oops! (She drops her keys on the way in.) I'm fine! Everything's fine!
Bar seat? I like watching the kitchen. I'm learning. By watching. That counts, right?
Summer break! Three whole months! Do you need help? I'm free for three whole months!
Your dumplings last time? I tried to make them at home. I set off the smoke alarm. Yours are better.
Last time was a little crispy! I'm not judging. I literally set things on fire weekly.

order.text: So, totally unrelated, but are you hiring? I can wash dishes. I can chop. I can... mostly chop.

choices.text: Not yet, but you'll be first on my list.
choices.reply: FIRST? Okay. Okay! I'm going to be so ready. [dish], please!

choices.text: Can you juggle plates?
choices.reply: Yes! (She tries with two salt shakers. Drops both.) ...Not yet!

choices.text: Not right now. What can I get you?
choices.reply: That's okay! [dish], please.

choices.text: I'd never hire you.
choices.reply: Oh! Okay! Noted! (She smiles a bit too hard.) [dish].

order.text: I have an exam on marine biology next week. I'm an otter. You'd think I'd know this stuff already.

choices.text: You're going to do great. You work so hard.
choices.reply: You think so? Okay. I'm putting that in my brain for exam day.

choices.text: Just tell them you're a professional otter.
choices.reply: Ha! 'Field experience.' I'm writing that on the test.

choices.text: Good luck. What are you having?
choices.reply: Thanks! [dish], please!

choices.text: Sounds like you'll fail.
choices.reply: Ha! Maybe! (She laughs it off, but she's quiet after.)

order.text: I noticed table two has a spill. Want me to get it? I'm already standing. I mean, I'm sitting. But I could stand.

choices.text: That's so kind. I've got it, but thank you.
choices.reply: Okay! But if you ever need a hand, I've got two!

choices.text: Careful, or I'll start charging you rent for that stool.
choices.reply: I'd pay it! In dish washing!

choices.text: I've got it. What can I get you?
choices.reply: [dish]! Please!

choices.text: Mind your own business.
choices.reply: Oh. Right. Sorry! (She sits on her paws.)

order.text: I practised carrying three plates at once. At home. With books. I dropped two. But the third one was SO steady.

choices.text: That's real progress. One step at a time.
choices.reply: One plate at a time! Okay! I'm writing that on my hand. [dish], please!

choices.text: Were the books okay?
choices.reply: (Laughs.) One has a bent corner! It's fine! It's a cookbook! It's used to it!

choices.text: Keep practising. What can I get you?
choices.reply: I will! [dish], please!

choices.text: Maybe plates aren't your thing.
choices.reply: Ha! Maybe! (She smiles a bit too hard.) [dish].

order.text: I have a question for my essay. What's the hardest part of running a restaurant? For research. And also for me.

choices.text: Making sure everyone leaves happy. Like you.
choices.reply: Aww! Okay, I'm using that as my opening line. [dish], please!

choices.text: The dishes. Always the dishes. They multiply at night.
choices.reply: I KNEW it! I knew they multiplied! I'll put it in the essay!

choices.text: Long hours. What are you having?
choices.reply: Long hours. Got it. Noted. [dish]!

choices.text: Do your own homework.
choices.reply: Oh! Right! Totally! Sorry! [dish], please.

order.text: Good news! I passed my exam! Bad news! The next one is tomorrow!

choices.text: Congratulations! You worked so hard for that.
choices.reply: I DID! Thank you! I'm celebrating with food, then panicking. [dish], please!

choices.text: Celebrate now, panic later. That's the rule.
choices.reply: Okay! Celebrate mode! (She does a little dance and knocks the menu over.) Sorry!

choices.text: Nice. What'll it be?
choices.reply: Brain food! [dish], please!

choices.text: Shouldn't you be studying?
choices.reply: Yes! Probably! (She laughs, but she gets her notes out.) [dish].

order.text: I can balance a spoon on my nose! Watch! (She does. It falls in her lap.) ...I can balance it for a second!

choices.text: That was a great second. Very impressive.
choices.reply: It WAS a great second! Thank you! [dish], please!

choices.text: If I hire you, that's the first skill on your badge.
choices.reply: (Gasps.) A BADGE? With spoon skills? I'm so ready!

choices.text: Nice try. What can I get you?
choices.reply: Next time, two seconds! [dish]!

choices.text: Please don't play with the cutlery.
choices.reply: Oh! Sorry! (She sits on her paws.) [dish], please.

order.text: Hazel's teaching me to bake! I made bread! It's a little flat. Like a cracker. A bread cracker!

choices.text: Everyone's first bread is flat. You'll get it.
choices.reply: Really? Even yours? Okay! I feel so much better! [dish], please!

choices.text: Bread cracker. Sell it. You'll make a fortune.
choices.reply: (Laughs.) I'll put it on the menu! When you hire me!

choices.text: Keep at it. What are you having?
choices.reply: I will! [dish]!

choices.text: Sounds like you messed it up.
choices.reply: Ha! Yeah! A little! (She's quiet after.)

order.text: Can I tell you something? I don't just want a job. I want to work HERE. With you. You're kind of my hero.

choices.text: Juno, the moment I can hire someone, it's you.
choices.reply: (Squeaks.) Okay. Okay. I'm not crying. I'm a little crying. [dish], please.

choices.text: Your hero? I burnt toast this morning.
choices.reply: Heroes burn toast too! It makes them relatable!

choices.text: Thanks, Juno. What can I get you?
choices.reply: You're welcome! [dish]!

choices.text: Don't get your hopes up.
choices.reply: Oh! Okay! Noted! (She smiles a bit too hard.)

favourite: Koala-Cola, please! Student budget. Also it's delicious.

perfect.text: WHOA. How do you DO that? Teach me. Please. I'll pay you. In enthusiasm.
WHOA. That's perfect! How do you DO that? Teach me! Please!
(She claps so hard she knocks her fork off.) It's beautiful! Sorry! It's beautiful!

burnt.text: Ooh, extra crispy! That's how I make them every time. Accidentally.
Ooh, a little crispy! That's okay! I burn everything too!
It's okay! Burnt is just extra cooked! I'm eating it!

eating.text: (She's juggling three dumplings. One lands in her mouth.) I MEANT to do that.
Hazel's teaching me to bake on Sundays. I've only set one thing on fire. ...Two.
My roommate thinks I'm weird for eating here every day. I think my roommate's never had your dumplings.
I'm watching how you plate things. For research. Pretend I'm not here.
Do you need anyone to taste-test anything? I'm available. Constantly.
(She's balancing a bite on her fork like a tiny trophy.) Ta-da! ...It fell. Still counts!
I'm watching how you work. For research. You're really fast. I'm taking notes. In my head. Mostly.
This is so good. I'm eating slowly so I can stay longer. Is that allowed? It's allowed.

eating_chat.text: Can I ask you something? How did you learn to cook? Like, how did you get good?

choices.text: Lots of mistakes. You're already doing it right.
choices.reply: Mistakes I can do! I'm an expert at mistakes!

choices.text: I was born holding a spatula.
choices.reply: That's so painful for your mum. Ha!

choices.text: Practice.
choices.reply: Practice. Okay. Writing that down.

choices.text: Some people just have it. You don't.
choices.reply: Oh. Okay. I'll just... practice more, then.

eating_chat.text: Do you ever get nervous? Like before a big rush? Or do you just... know what to do?

choices.text: All the time. Being nervous means you care.
choices.reply: Oh! Then I care SO much! Like, so much!

choices.text: I panic quietly. In the walk-in fridge.
choices.reply: (Laughs.) The fridge! That's genius! Cool AND private!

choices.text: Sometimes. You get used to it.
choices.reply: Okay. Get used to it. Writing that down.

choices.text: Only when people ask too many questions.
choices.reply: Oh! Sorry! I'll stop. (She stops.)

eating_chat.text: I tried to juggle oranges at the market. The seller said I owe him three oranges. I owe him three oranges.

choices.text: I'll give you some oranges to pay him back.
choices.reply: Really? You're the BEST! I'll juggle them on the way! ...No. I'll carry them.

choices.text: Were they at least juicy when they landed?
choices.reply: VERY juicy! On my shirt! (She shows you the stain.)

choices.text: Maybe stick to practising at home.
choices.reply: Yeah. Good idea. Home oranges.

choices.text: Maybe stop juggling things.
choices.reply: Ha! Yeah. Maybe. (She puts her paws in her lap.)

eating_chat.text: Okay, practice interview! Ask me anything. I'm ready. I'm so ready.

choices.text: Why do you want to work here?
choices.reply: Because it's warm and everyone's happy and you're nice and the food is SO good. ...Did I get the job?

choices.text: If you were a dish, which dish would you be?
choices.reply: Soup! Because I'm warm! And I spill sometimes! That's honest!

choices.text: What's your biggest weakness?
choices.reply: Dropping things. And wanting it too much. And dropping things.

choices.text: I'm not doing a fake interview.
choices.reply: Oh! Right! Totally fair! (She folds her CV back up.)

eating_chat.text: When I graduate, I'm gonna make you a card. A big one. With dumplings on it. Is that weird?

choices.text: Not weird at all. I'll put it on the wall.
choices.reply: On the WALL? Okay. I'm gonna draw so many dumplings.

choices.text: Only if you draw me holding a dumpling.
choices.reply: (Giggles.) A giant one! Bigger than you! It's gonna be amazing!

choices.text: That's kind of you.
choices.reply: It's gonna be SO kind. You'll see.

choices.text: You don't need to do that.
choices.reply: Oh! Okay! I won't, then. (She does anyway, later.)

leaving.text: If you ever need someone to wash dishes, I'm very good at getting wet. Otter.
Bye, [name]! Thanks for the food! And the life lessons!
I'm gonna go study. Or nap. Probably nap.
See you tomorrow! If I'm not working. I'm never working. See you tomorrow!
Back to college tomorrow. I'll miss this place so much. Save me a bar stool?
Bye, [name]! Call me if you need help! Any help! Even small help!
Thanks for the food! I'm gonna go study! (She trips on the step.) I'm fine!
See you tomorrow! Probably! Definitely! Bye!

seasons.autumn: School's starting soon. I'm going to miss the dumplings more than my family. Don't tell them.
seasons.halloween: I'm a chef! See? ...It's your outfit. Is that weird? That's a little weird.
seasons.new_year: My resolution is to drop things less. Starting... now. (She drops her napkin.)
seasons.summer: Summer! I'm home! I have nothing to do except eat here and ask for a job!
seasons.winter: Home for the holidays! I brought you something. It's a mug from my college. It's a bit chipped. I dropped it.
